4. It is further stated that the plaintiff suddenly went to the suit land and found a sign board in the names defendants Nos. 1 to 3 Md. Yusuf Shikder, Mst. Momtaz Begum and Akhter Hossain Sikder along with their address in the suit land on 18.1.2000: that then the plaintiff went to the residences of defendants No. 1 to 3 and found defendant No. 2 Mst. Momtaz Begum who claimed that they purchased the suit land from the plaintiff but defendant No.2 failed to recognize the plaintiff; and that thereafter the plaintiff paid necessary money to a deed writer to get a certified copy of the sale deed, if any, was executed and registered in the names of defendants Nos. 1 to 3 on 18.01. 2000 and he found sale deed No. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 on search and obtained a certified copy of the said sale deed on 20.01.2000 and got it on 02.02.2000. It is further stated that on scrum"' of the said deed of sale, the plaintiff found it a false deed as he did not execute and register it and the attesting witnesses were not known to him and he did not receive consideration money from the defendants and even the plaintiff did not appear before the sub-registrar office; that the defendants Nos. 1 to 3 created a false deed of sale bearing No.2826 on 12.08.1996 by using his false signatures and then he requested defendants Nos. 1 to 3 to cancel the said deed but they did not lend cars ' to the request of the plaintiff. Thereafter the plaintiff threw away the sign-board of the defendants from the suit land and he placed a sign board of his name in the suit land. It is further stated that deed of sale no. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 case a cloud in the title of the plaintiff in the suit land and as-such the plaintiff was constrained to institute Title Suit No.40 of 2000 which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.106 of 2001 for cancellation of sale deed on 17.02.2000. It is noted that thereafter the defendants Nos. 1 to 3 taking advantage of the abnormal political situation prevailing in the country, dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land and constructed thatched huts thereon and as such the plaintiff amended the plaint of the suit by inserting the prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit property. 

 18. Mr. Ahsanullah further submits that as the suit land is not identical with the purchased land of the petitioner that is why the defendants opposite parties filed an application for appointing a survey knowing advocate Commissioner in order to relay the petitioner's purchased land with suit land but the learned trial court rejected the prayer. He further submits that suit land is not identical with the purchased land of the petitioner and moreover the interested persons were not made parties in the suit, so the plaintiff petitioner cannot get a decree for declaration and khas possession. He further submits that ends of justice will be met if suit is sent back on remand with direction to make the interested persons parties, to take their deeds into evidence and to relay the suit land with the purchased land. 

 20. In plain reading of the plaint, it appears to us that plaintiff petitioner firstly filed suit for declaring the kabala no. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 forged, ' void, inoperative fraudulent and illegal and later on the amended the plaint for declaration title and for khas possession along with earlier relief as he was dispossessed from the suit land. 

 24. If the court wants to declare the disputed kabala illegal and void, it is to be decided as to whether the suit land is identical with land of disputed kabalas. In order to declare the title of the plaintiff and to give him khas possession, it is to be decided first as to whether the salt land and the purchased land of plaintiff is identical or not.
